dispositions.note: FR-011 says bridge runtime configuration includes "audience, expected service account, OIDC verifier" and gates activation through a manifest, but omits the subscription value required by provider-shadow-ingress.ts:213 to validate envelope.subscription.
FR-002: "enqueue {history_id} durably BEFORE acknowledging"; FR-011 likewise requires "durable-enqueue-before-ack" before activation.

FR-011 still does not compose: the hub relays under x-webhook-bridge-secret, while the bridge contract still requires Google OIDC Bearer and an OIDC verifier. Current relay.ts:45-66 sends no Authorization header, and provider-shadow-ingress.ts:209-216 requires one.
G-19 now says the hub serves /healthz and /webhooks/:name for zoom-officehours, ops-check-lead, and fireflies, with no Gmail integration.

G-22 correctly says history IDs are typically valid for a week but sometimes only hours, and FR-002 handles 404, but "enqueue a full-window sweep" means the default three-day window unless otherwise sized; it does not guarantee recovery of the entire cursor gap.
G-23 now states that SystemExit(5) applies only when participants and text_units are both absent, classification is optional, and planned_files is meeting-shaped.
G-28 now limits the absence claim to gcloud/configuration and records the readable project and service-account identities.
G-32 explicitly records a later 2026-09-15 re-probe reporting launchd running and three HTTP 200 health responses; the earlier stopped observation is no longer presented as current.
G-33 now identifies the webhook-hub repository's separate Railway link and lists its production variable names.

FR-002 correctly lists history from last_processed_history_id and advances only after processing, but its first-run bootstrap uses users.getProfile after the triggering push. That cursor is already at or beyond the notification watermark, so the first Tier-B event can return zero history and be lost.

FR-002 now follows nextPageToken, deduplicates IDs, and defines zero-result advancement, but still specifies no bounded chunk/checkpoint scheme or receipt counts for pages, records, unique IDs, and remaining work.

FR-002 gives the detached drain's complete required path argv: --repo-root, --vault, --crm-dir, and --state-dir; G-25 correctly preserves live mode as absence of --dry-run and names the new flags as implementation work.
FR-002 says last_success_at/window_days/message_count are written only by completed full-window sweeps and gives event runs separate receipt fields.
FR-009 checks launchd state, last_pull freshness, and stuck queue depth, and forbids one-line OK whenever trigger health is DOWN/STALE.

FR-003 correctly forbids declaring FREE_MAIL domains and proposes exact-contact/company binding, but that fallback depends on contact auto-creation that unchanged base FR-006 permits only for a domain-matched sender.
FR-003 defines one predicate requiring INBOX, retained labelIds/raw headers, in:inbox on sweeps, and local rejection for by-ID entry forms.

FR-003 defines a parity fixture, fail-closed handling, and predicate-divergence telemetry, but runtime sweep processing can detect only query-admitted/local-rejected IDs; it cannot observe the stated "vice versa" case without a broader oracle query.
FR-005 explicitly says both known-entity/volume sentences are SUPERSEDED and restates the no-tools, schema, budget, task-routing, and digest containment rules.
FR-003 specifies stage-1 and final-binding identities, stage-1 binding precedence on drift, both-call budgeting, and caching on the append-only row history.
FR-003 requires writeback_email.create_page and explicitly says "NOT writeback_render.planned_files," while defining template, domains, CRM-name, and History responsibilities.
FR-001 adds created:<vault-relative path> to writes, and FR-003/FR-009 require it to render as created.
FR-003 requires checking both clients/<slug>.md and orgs/<slug>.md plus identity maps, reusing only on identity match and otherwise allocating a disambiguated slug.
FR-003 says internal/colleague is valid only for OURS_DOMAINS and escalates an external-domain internal classification.
FR-011 gates active mode on all five prerequisites, including a machine-consulted activation manifest; provider-config.json alone cannot activate Tier B.
FR-011 names projects/cortextos-gws-495505/topics/<name> and requires exact equality with the credential project executing users.watch.
FR-002 requires queueing plus detached subprocess.Popen without waiting and a fake-clock regression comparing prefilter decisions, pending_since, attention argv, and spawn timing.

FR-003 defines an email-local evidence gate using normalize_quote/quote_grounded over body plus From/Subject and mandates escalation for invalid or ungrounded classification; both helpers exist in resolve_meeting.py.

new_findings.claim: FR-003 simultaneously requires every admitted inbound real-person message to be filed and requires admitted personal messages to be ignored with no page or CRM write.
new_findings.evidence: FR-003: "System MUST file every INBOUND message that passes the real-person filter" versus "personal ⇒ observation with outcome ignored, reason personal, no page, no CRM write"; A-08 repeats the exception.
new_findings.fix: Amend the top-level MUST and D-11 to state the precise personal exception, or require a home for personal messages.

new_findings.claim: The free-mail binding path cannot be implemented under the unchanged CRM-write requirement.
new_findings.evidence: FR-003 requires FREE_MAIL senders to bind through "contact auto-create per base FR-006"; base FR-006 permits auto-creation only "when a domain-matched sender has no contact row." FREE_MAIL senders deliberately receive no declared domain match.
new_findings.fix: Explicitly amend FR-006 to permit classification-backed contact creation for admitted free-mail senders, including interaction and rollback/idempotency semantics, or introduce a separate exact-address binding store.

new_findings.claim: Tier B can acknowledge and lose its first notification because the initial history cursor is bootstrapped after the event.
new_findings.evidence: FR-002: "list history from the per-mailbox last_processed_history_id ... bootstrapped from users.getProfile on first run" and then advance to the queued watermark. Gmail history.list returns changes after the start cursor; a post-notification profile cursor is already equal to or newer than that watermark.
new_findings.fix: Persist the historyId returned by users.watch before enabling push delivery and use it as the initial prior cursor. Never initialize from a post-notification profile cursor; if no prior cursor exists, run a gap-sized recovery sweep before acknowledging or advancing.
